passages.t: The gatekeepers, and the gates by lot
passages.happening:
The divisions of the gatekeepers come from the Korahites and the Merarites (verses 1-11). Obed-edom has eight sons, ‘For God had blessed Obed-edom’ (verse 5), and his family numbers sixty-two capable men (verse 8). Hosah's son Shimri is made first although he was not the firstborn (verse 10).

‘They cast lots for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike’ (verse 13). ‘The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and the lot for the North Gate fell to him’ (verse 14). Obed-edom takes the south and the storehouse, Shuppim and Hosah the west, and guards are posted at every watch (verses 15-19).
passages.hearers:
The organizing of the temple goes on: Levites, priests, musicians, and now the gatekeepers. Chapter 27 will finish with the army and the officers of the kingdom. By the end, every part of the temple's service, from the altar to the doors, is in place before Solomon lays a stone. Who to notice: Obed-edom, and the wise counselor Zechariah.

Obed-edom is presumably the man in whose house the ark stayed for three months, where the LORD did good to his household (13:14). His large family here is the Chronicler's evidence of that favor. The Korahites belonged to the clan of Kohath, the family linked with the sons of Korah in the Psalms. The Asaph of verse 1 is probably not the musician of chapter 25, who was of Gershon's line; many take him to be the Korahite Ebiasaph named in chapters 6 and 9.

Gatekeepers were more than doormen. They controlled who came into the temple courts, kept out the unclean and the unauthorized, guarded the storerooms and kept order. The east gate faced the temple's entrance and had the largest guard. The word for gate, shaar, also names a place of defense and of judgment. The roster repeats capable men, chayil, a word for strength, worth and excellence of character, and it notices a wise counselor and a son appointed first by his father's choice. Character and ability counted alongside descent.
passages.later: A psalm of the sons of Korah says, ‘I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked’ (Psalm 84:10). After the exile the returning families included ‘The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum’ (Ezra 2:42) and others.
passages.asks: The doorkeepers were chosen for strength and wisdom, and a psalm says a doorkeeper's place in God's house is better than any other. Ask whether you would be glad of the doorway rather than the center. And ask who keeps the doors of your church, and whether they know they are seen.

passages.t: Treasurers, and officers beyond the temple
passages.happening:
‘Now their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things’ (verse 20). Shelomith and his brothers keep the gifts dedicated by David, the family heads and the army commanders, who ‘had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD’ (verse 27). ‘Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah’ (verse 28) is in their care.

Other Levites have duties outside the temple as officers and judges over Israel (verse 29). Hebronites with 1,700 capable men oversee the land west of the Jordan, ‘for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king’ (verse 30). In David's fortieth year capable men are found among the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead, and David appoints 2,700 of them over the tribes east of the Jordan (verses 31-32).
passages.hearers:
In the ancient world, temples were treasuries as well as places of worship. Gifts and spoils dedicated to a god were stored there and guarded carefully. The word otsar means both the treasury and the treasure. What was dedicated, qadash, moved from ordinary use into God's possession, and the Levites who kept it held a trust.

The list of givers gathers Israel's history into the house of God: Samuel the seer, Saul, Abner, Joab and David. Men who opposed each other in life, Saul and David, Abner and Joab, all have their gifts in the same treasury.

Verse 31 dates the search of the records to David's fortieth year, his last, which fits these chapters at the end of his life. Jazer in Gilead lay east of the Jordan. Levites served outside the temple too, as officers and judges in the land, and the phrase for the work of the LORD and for the service of the king shows worship and government working together across the kingdom. Gatekeepers remained an important order after the exile.
passages.later: King Jehoshaphat later set Levites to serve in the same way, saying, ‘And the Levites will serve as officers before you’ (2 Chronicles 19:11). At Jericho Joshua had said of the spoil, ‘all the silver and gold and all the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they must go into His treasury’ (Joshua 6:19).
passages.asks: Saul, Abner, Joab and David, men who fought one another, all left gifts in God's house. Ask what you would want to leave there. And ask whether there is someone you have opposed whose gift to God you need to honor.
